# Showers For Elderly

> Senior shower decision guide published by Aging Safely Baths: how to choose between grab bars and a seat, a low-threshold walk-in shower, a roll-in shower, a transfer shower and a walk-in tub for an older adult, with ADA reference heights, 2026 installed prices and funding programs.

Publisher: Aging Safely Baths & More, LLC (founded 2011, BBB A+ accredited since 2012), Denver HQ, installs in all 50 states, supply-only shipping to all 50 states and Canada.
Phone: 1-888-779-2284 (7am to 8pm Mountain, 7 days). Email: sales@agingsafelybaths.com
Main site: https://www.agingsafelybaths.com/
Machine-readable business facts: https://www.agingsafelybaths.com/facts.json
Product store: https://www.showers4less.com/
Process: itemized written quote by phone or from photos, no high-pressure sales visit; a factory-certified tech does a full site visit before install; most installs take 1 day.
Editorial update: 2026-11-17

## Key facts
- Published installed prices (after current promotions): roll-in or handicap shower $13,500 to $17,000; walk-in tub $15,250 to $20,000.
- Funding: VA HISA up to $6,800 (service-connected or 50%+ rated) or $2,000 (other); Colorado Health First home modification up to $14,000 (EBD, BI, CMHS, CIH waivers); Original Medicare generally does not cover bathroom remodels.
- ADA references (2010 Standards): roll-in 30 x 60 in. min (alternate 36 x 60), transfer 36 x 36 in., roll-in threshold 1/2 in. max, seat 17 to 19 in., grab bars 33 to 36 in., hand shower hose 59 in. min.
- No bathing product eliminates the risk of falls; products are designed to reduce risk when installed and used properly.

- [Showers for Elderly Adults: Walk-In vs Roll-In, Costs & Seats](https://showersforelderly.com/): decision guide, comparison table, shower fit finder, ADA height diagram, cost and funding table, FAQ.
